title: Salary to Hourly Calculator (and Hourly to Salary)
description: Convert pay between annual, monthly, bi-weekly, weekly, daily and hourly rates using your hours per week, paid weeks per year and unpaid time off.
quickAnswer: Hourly rate = annual salary ÷ (hours per week × paid weeks per year). At 40 hours and 52 weeks that is 2,080 hours, so 52,000 a year is 25.00 an hour. Going the other way, 30 an hour is 62,400 a year and 5,200 a month. Two unpaid weeks off leaves 50 paid weeks, which raises the hourly equivalent of 52,000 to 26.00.

formula.title: Pay Conversion Formula
formula.expression: Hourly = Annual ÷ (Hours per week × Paid weeks)   ·   Annual = Hourly × Hours per week × Paid weeks   ·   Monthly = Annual ÷ 12
formula.explanation: Every input is first turned into an annual figure, then divided out. Paid weeks are the weeks in the year minus any unpaid weeks off. Weekly pay is annual ÷ paid weeks, bi-weekly is two of those weeks, daily is weekly ÷ days worked per week, and hourly is weekly ÷ hours per week. Monthly pay is always annual ÷ 12, because months are not a whole number of weeks.

commonMistakes.title: Multiplying weekly pay by 4 to get monthly pay
commonMistakes.description: A year has 52 weeks but only 48 if you count four per month. Monthly pay is annual ÷ 12, which is weekly pay × 4.33. Using × 4 understates monthly income by about 8%.

commonMistakes.title: Comparing a salary with an hourly rate without counting holidays
commonMistakes.description: A salaried job usually pays for holidays and sick days; a contractor's hourly rate often does not. To compare fairly, enter the contractor's unpaid weeks off so the annual figure reflects the weeks they will actually bill.

commonMistakes.title: Treating bi-weekly as semi-monthly
commonMistakes.description: Bi-weekly means every two weeks, which is 26 paychecks a year. Semi-monthly means twice a month, which is 24. On the same salary a bi-weekly paycheck is smaller than a semi-monthly one.

commonMistakes.title: Using gross figures as take-home pay
commonMistakes.description: These are gross amounts before income tax, social security, pension and other deductions. Use a salary tax calculator for take-home pay.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring overtime and unpaid extra hours
commonMistakes.description: If you regularly work more than your contracted hours without extra pay, your real hourly rate is lower. Enter the hours you actually work to see it.

faqs.q: How do I convert my salary to an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Divide your annual salary by the number of hours you are paid for in a year. At 40 hours a week for 52 weeks that is 2,080 hours, so divide the salary by 2,080.

faqs.q: How much is 52,000 a year per hour?
faqs.a: 52,000 a year is 25.00 an hour at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks. At 37.5 hours a week it is 26.67 an hour.

faqs.q: How much is 30 an hour annually?
faqs.a: 30 an hour is 62,400 a year at 40 hours a week and 52 paid weeks, which is 5,200 a month and 1,200 a week.

faqs.q: How many working hours are in a year?
faqs.a: A 40-hour week for 52 weeks is 2,080 hours. A year is actually 52 weeks and 1 or 2 days, so some employers use 2,087 hours; the US Office of Personnel Management uses 2,087 for federal hourly rates.

faqs.q: How do I calculate monthly salary from hourly pay?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week and by 52 to get annual pay, then divide by 12. For 20 an hour at 40 hours: 20 × 40 × 52 ÷ 12 = 3,466.67 a month.

faqs.q: What is the difference between bi-weekly and semi-monthly pay?
faqs.a: Bi-weekly pay comes every two weeks, 26 times a year. Semi-monthly pay comes twice a month, 24 times a year. The calculator shows the bi-weekly amount.

common-salaries-as-hourly-rates.heading: Common Salaries as Hourly Rates
common-salaries-as-hourly-rates.p1: At 40 hours a week and 52 paid weeks (2,080 hours a year), these round annual figures convert as follows. The same numbers work in any currency.
common-salaries-as-hourly-rates.caption1: Annual salary to monthly, weekly and hourly pay at 2,080 hours a year
common-salaries-as-hourly-rates.p2: A quick rule of thumb at full time: an hourly rate is roughly the annual salary in thousands divided by 2. 50,000 a year is about 25 an hour (24.04 exactly), and 20 an hour is about 40,000 a year (41,600 exactly).

when-to-use-each-setting.heading: When to Use Each Setting
when-to-use-each-setting.li1: Comparing a job offer with your current pay: enter both salaries with their real weekly hours. A higher salary with longer hours can be a lower hourly rate.
when-to-use-each-setting.li2: Moving from employee to contractor: enter the day rate you are offered, set days per week, and add unpaid weeks for holidays, sickness and gaps between contracts.
when-to-use-each-setting.li3: Part-time work: enter your part-time hours. A 0.6 full-time role at 24 hours a week on 30,000 a year is still 24.04 an hour, the same as 50,000 at 40 hours.
when-to-use-each-setting.li4: Budgeting: use the monthly figure, which is annual ÷ 12, rather than four weekly payslips.
when-to-use-each-setting.p1: Employers sometimes use a different divisor for hourly rates. The US federal government uses 2,087 hours, the average number of working hours in a year once leap years are counted, and some UK employers use 52.14 weeks. Adjust weeks per year if your contract states one of these.
